name: OpenMP parallel nearest-neighbor distance (The C++ Programmer's Mindset)
listed_description: Brute-force closest-pair distance over 2D points, outer loop parallelized with an OpenMP min reduction, compared against the same sequential loop.
claim_text: About 4x faster with 8 threads on 65,536 points: 4,797 ms sequential versus 1,161 ms with OpenMP.
book_benchmark: 65,536 Point2D values, 8 threads, sequential loop baseline; compiler, flags and CPU not stated in the chunk.
found_in: book: The C++ Programmer's Mindset (2025), ch. 4, section 'Processor threads' (code in Chapter-04 folder)

name: Cache-blocked matrix multiplication with tile accumulator (The C++ Programmer's Mindset)
listed_description: Blocked (tiled) GEMM-style routine with block size 32 and a small temporary tile that stays in low-level cache, compared with the naive triple loop and with OpenBLAS.
claim_text: Basic algorithm 547 ms, blocked (block size 32) 289 ms, OpenBLAS 24.1 ms per multiplication.
book_benchmark: Square double matrices (size shown only in an image); average of 39 iterations (basic), 73 (blocked), 874 (OpenBLAS); compiler, flags and CPU not stated in the chunk.
guessed_baseline: naive triple-loop matrix multiply; OpenBLAS is the faster reference
found_in: book: The C++ Programmer's Mindset (2025), ch. 4, section 'Matrix multiplication with cache in mind'

name: SAXPY function multiversioning with target_clones and manual CPUID dispatch (The C++ Programmer's Mindset)
listed_description: Same auto-vectorized saxpy loop compiled for default, SSE4.2, AVX2 and AVX-512F, selected at runtime by target_clones or a hand-written CPUID dispatcher; also a hand-crafted intrinsics version and an OpenBLAS comparison.
claim_text: Vector size 5120: default 329 ns, sse4.2 330 ns, hand-crafted 298 ns, avx2 259 ns, avx512f 243 ns; OpenBLAS saxpy 278 ns.
book_benchmark: saxpy on 5120 floats, averaged runs; baseline is the default (SSE2) build; GCC -O3 implied; CPU not stated in the chunk. Book warns OpenBLAS overhead may distort this small size.
guessed_baseline: default SSE2 auto-vectorized saxpy; OpenBLAS saxpy
found_in: book: The C++ Programmer's Mindset (2025), ch. 4, section 'SIMD'

name: Clamp loop with conditional store (The C++ Programmer's Mindset)
listed_description: Clamp uint16_t values to 255 by storing only when a value exceeds the maximum (with an unlikely hint), so the CPU can speculate past the store; compared with the conditional-move version.
claim_text: Average 605 ns for the cmov-based clamp_min versus 500 ns for clamp_conditional, on 1,000 uniformly random uint16_t values.
book_benchmark: 1,000 uint16_t values uniformly in 0..65535; GCC assembly shown; flags and CPU not stated in the chunk. Book says the improvement is modest and to measure first.
guessed_baseline: branchless conditional-move clamp compiled by GCC
found_in: book: The C++ Programmer's Mindset (2025), ch. 4, section 'Branch prediction and speculative execution'
